original_question: In the same setting where X is a nonsingular projective variety over C, M_g(X, beta) is the moduli space of stable maps, pi: M_g(X, beta) -> M_g is the forgetful morphism, and [M_g(X, beta)]^vir is the virtual class, for which targets X and curve classes beta does the Chow-theoretic pushforward pi_*([M_g(X, beta)]^vir) lie in the tautological subring of A_*(M_g)?
target_in_paper: Q2 in part (i), "On the virtual class": "When does \pi_*[\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}} \in A^*(\overline{M}_g) lie in the tautological ring in Chow?"
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper's Chow-theoretic question about the pushforward of the virtual fundamental class along the forgetful map from the moduli of stable maps to the moduli of curves. It also keeps the essential data appearing in the paper: a nonsingular projective target X over \mathbf{C}, a curve class \beta, the moduli space of stable maps, the virtual class, and the issue of tautologicality on the moduli of curves.
missing_details: The paper uses the compactified moduli spaces \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) and \overline{M}_g, not the open loci M_g(X,\beta) and M_g.
The genus g is part of the fixed data in the question; your draft asks only for which X and \beta, but the paper's formulation is really about the class attached to a given g as well.
The morphism \pi is the usual forgetful morphism to the moduli of stable curves, i.e. forgetting the map and stabilizing the domain.

The paper phrases the target as the Chow ring A^*(\overline{M}_g) and asks whether the class lies in the tautological ring there; your draft instead says A_*(M_g), which is close in spirit but not the paper's literal formulation.
The paper asks about the pushforward of the bare virtual class only; it does not include insertions, descendants, or marked points in Q2.
The immediately following context matters: the paper says the answer to Q2 is not yes in general, and that counterexamples already occur when X is a curve.
The only specific positive criterion suggested in the paper is the author's 'wild speculation' that Q2 should hold when X is defined over \overline{\mathbf{Q}}.
The note does not impose any additional positivity, degree, or ampleness hypotheses on \beta; it is simply the curve class determining \overline{M}_g(X,\beta).
refined_question: Fix a genus g, a nonsingular projective variety X over \mathbf{C}, and a curve class \beta on X. Let \pi:\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)\to\overline{M}_g be the forgetful morphism from the moduli space of stable maps to the moduli space of stable curves, and let [\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}} be its virtual fundamental class. When does the Chow pushforward \pi_*([\overline{M}_g(X,\beta)]^{\mathrm{vir}}) belong to the tautological ring R^*(\overline{M}_g)\subset A^*(\overline{M}_g)? In particular, is this always the case when X is defined over \overline{\mathbf{Q}}, as suggested in the paper?
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's Q2 in part (i), not a neighboring problem: it asks exactly for the Chow-tautologicality of the pushforward of the virtual class under the stable-map forgetful morphism. To make the question fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, the rewrite restores the compactified notation \overline{M}_g(X,\beta) and \overline{M}_g from the setup preceding Q1 and Q2, treats g as part of the fixed input, and matches the paper's literal Chow-ring formulation A^*(\overline{M}_g). I also folded in the paper's immediate clarification of intent after Q2: the statement is false in general, with counterexamples already for curve targets, and the only concrete positive direction proposed there is the speculation for targets defined over \overline{\mathbf{Q}}.
